Take a look at this diagram showing the difference between sine, cosine, and tangent. In the situation you've described, we would select the tangent triangle and place two of them side by side, just as the triangle is now. We've selected tan because we know what the angles are for each observer and we know the distance between them on the ground (we know the adjacent length). The equation for tan is TOA, or tan = opposite/adjacent.

Now, starting with the right triangle (observer A); we know that the angle is 20 degrees (since they're both west of the plane, the person closest will have a larger angle, a sharper view upward, to see the plane), and we would state that equation as tan 20 = O/A

On the left triangle (observer B); we know that the angle is 13 degrees, and we also know that the two people are 3 miles apart, so the equation becomes tan 13 = O/(A+3 miles).

Since we want to know how high the airplane is, we solve for O. Start off by setting the equations equal to each other. You have to rewrite them first.

  • tan 20 = O/A --> A = O/tan 20
  • tan 13 = O/(A+3miles) --> A = (O/tan 13) - 3

Now that they equal each other, you're saying

  • O/tan 20 = (O/tan 13) - 3.

Solve

edit (to add note and for formatting): check out Khan Academy for help with math and loads of other stuff. It is an extremely useful resource and you will see multiple ways of solving problems.

Here is a graphic of the situation. And Here is a handwritten version of the following solution.

STEP 1: Solve for the inner angles.

[;\alpha=180^\circ-20^\circ=160^\circ;]

[;\beta=180^\circ-\alpha-13^\circ=180^\circ-173^\circ=7^\circ;]

 

STEP 2: Solve the side length BC.

Using the sine law:

[;\frac{BC}{\sin{\alpha}}=\frac{3}{\sin{\beta}}\rightarrow BC=\sin(160^\circ)\cdot\frac{3}{\sin(\7^\circ)}=8.419;] miles.

 

STEP 3: Solve for the height of the airplane.

Using the sine function, [;\sin(\theta)=\frac{opp}{hyp};], with BC as the hypotenuse, h as the opposite side, and 13° as the angle,

[;\sin(13^\circ)=\frac{h}{BC}\rightarrow h=8.419\cdot\sin(13^\circ)=1.89;] miles.
